# HachiShifter MLD5 integration (updated 2026-11-01)

Sources: the user-provided `G:/mld5/src` independent C++17 reconstruction plus the further `/home/ubuntu/hjs/melodyne5-re` WSL transition/stretch-control work (16 production modules). The new transition helper is NOT a complete native child/phase/queue implementation; its simplified identity/compatibility predicates and once-only counter do not grant waveform reuse or prove pending-empty. Its clock/reader evidence informs the Hachi integration without being advertised as a new complete audio renderer. Original DLLs, reference WAVs, IDA data, model weights, Python and research tools are not included or called. The supplied README, RESULTS and HACHISHIFTER_INTEGRATION documents retain the original evidence boundaries; their fixture/test/notes links refer to the full research project and are not shipped fixtures.

## Recovered vs host responsibilities

- Recovered DSP: exact-order period startup/selection, rolling readout, frame windows, packed FFT convention, component mask, processed ADD/OLA, sampled controls, source-time feedback and component shutdown/gain.
- Hachi input adapter: the existing analysed source MIDI and authored target MIDI, formant and gain are already on target time. The adapter converts only the source-period table to source time through the inverse map, not the target controls a second time.
- Hachi retains the native source PCM rate up to48kHz (higher-rate PCM is converted once), renders on the48kHz output grid and restores the original external rate/channel/frame count. It no longer forces48→32→48. The UV/original lane and processed lane meet on the SAME output grid before the one final rate conversion; entirely UV identity requests are exact PCM copies. This does NOT implement or claim Melodyne's original source separator/analysis.
- Identity clocks with constant Q and entirely voiced controls use the highest supplied `render_period_component_source_time_gain` composition, preserving the actual caller knots and endpoint/count feedback. No fixed fixture-specific knot positions or reference samples are embedded. The caller supplies the actual endpoint. Update207 corrects the earlier EOF policy: file/reader EOF is not a scheduler fact. Terminal-component, pending-empty and zero-remainder permissions must be explicitly supplied; unknown facts remain false and cannot bake a shutdown fade into a note cut.
- Nonidentity Hachi clocks and automated Q use the SAME recovered period/FFT/OLA core through `Mld5NativeControl`: persistent S/R/C, source endpoint-minus-current/count feedback, rate ramps and native UPDATED_R output ordering. It validates driver/controller advancement and keeps dynamic-Q components on a consistent processed-frame topology. Hidden carrier R/Q prewarm is distinct from audible UV gating. This host-control extension is functional integration, not evidence of original control-manager equivalence for arbitrary projects.
- Hachi's normal gain/expression/export pipeline remains authoritative. noteGain is applied once, with no fitted EQ or whole-clip RMS correction inside MLD5. MLD3 stays disabled. Virtual-group assembly and separated-component export retain their explicit unsupported guards rather than falling back to old MLD5 or another engine.

## Local modifications to the supplied library

1. Consumer CMake explicitly builds production sources only; strict floating-point options are private to the recovered library and the host adapter TU, not forced onto NSF/WORLD/other Hachi algorithms.
2. `detail::PeriodRendererRateControl` adds optional `frame_probe_ratio(defaultQ)` with a default returning the original constant. The period driver queries it before frame planning, selects FFT according to that Q and forwards it unchanged to the same spectral-frame processor. Existing source-time/cached/scalar compositions retain their original constant-Q behavior; no recovered kernel arithmetic, windows or OLA were replaced. A second default-false `requires_processed_frames()` seam keeps Hachi dynamic-Q frame topology stable without changing Q values or the native default.

## Scope and limitations

The upstream five frozen reference comparisons are its own results, not an accuracy claim for Hachi's different analysis/component inputs. The adapter supports finite forward source maps, positive analysed vocal periods and bounded pitch/formant ratios. Unsupported/reversed maps or failed native kernel calls return a render failure; no legacy spectral-remap, LLSM2 or WORLD replacement is hidden behind the MLD5 selection. This change does not enable full source assembly for MLD5 or claim full Melodyne 5 equivalence.

Update206 adds proven continuous-source sessions on their actual timeline union, one synthesis before owner slicing, and mixer-time single-coverage normalization on the common sample grid. Authored fades/gains remain separate. It does not merge independent same-file layers, conflicting clocks/control curves or arbitrary virtual assemblies. Update207 removes the order2 Signalsmith/RMS/declick cascade: source stretch stays in native S/dS, so a single compatible component can legitimately produce the same native output under both layouts. Independent components are not concatenated into an invented shared waveform. At true touches inside an already shared stream, paired successive-join weights are redundant (two disjoint half-fades create a dropout); remove only those weights, preserving user fadeIn/fadeOut, gains and real overlapping crossfades.

The actual4s vowel failure was sparse importer property coverage incorrectly turning a valid source-item tail into UV. Fresh imports use actual sample support and preserve explicit silent points. Legacy renders carry SAME-note source hints and explicit target intent separately; the Hachi source-analysis helper can restore only missing pairs backed by strong native PCM periodicity, without editing project data. Ambiguous/nonstationary tails remain unrecovered; no blind UV fill, source-filename rule, fixed octave change, EQ or gain fit is used. This is Hachi frontend evidence, NOT a recovered original detector.

Only the MLD5 audio/waveform cache key gets the new implementation revision `mld5-recovered-period-v5-voicing-join`; saved algorithm string `mld5`, enum and picker ID1 remain stable, and NSF remains the default.
